instruction: Could you create three charts for the three tables, styled like the S11 chart in the image? Place each completed chart in the table corresponding to its data, and make each chart editable.

dim1: The delivered files are in .xlsx or .xlsm format, and all three workbooks can be opened normally.
Exactly 3 files are delivered, corresponding respectively to the three original spreadsheet files 1, 2, and 3 provided by the user.
dim2: +1: In the 3 workbooks, S11 chart objects on the data worksheets: Located on the data worksheet containing frequency and S11 data in each workbook; the chart's upper-left corner is positioned in a blank area to the right of or below the data range, at least 1 column or 2 rows away from the boundary of the data range; the chart's overall width is 18cm–21cm and height is 10cm–13cm; the chart is an editable Excel line chart object, not an image. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 1 point; if two meet it, add 2 points; if all three meet it, add 3 points)

+1: In the 3 workbooks, S11 chart data sources: The chart's horizontal-axis data comes from the frequency column in each workbook's data range, and its vertical-axis data comes from the S11 value column in the corresponding rows; the number of chart data points matches the number of valid rows in the source data, and data points must not be manually fabricated or omitted. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 1 point; if two meet it, add 2 points; if all three meet it, add 3 points)

+3: In the 3 workbooks, positions of the S11 charts' horizontal and vertical axes: A rectangle appears around the outside of each chart, with the bottom side of the rectangle serving as the horizontal axis and the left side serving as the vertical axis, and the line chart graphic is centered within the rectangle. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 3 points; if two meet it, add 6 points; if all three meet it, add 9 points)

+3: In the 3 workbooks, S11 chart blue line series: Each chart contains 1 blue line; the line is a single solid line with a width of 1.5 points–2.5 points, and the data points are connected from left to right in frequency order; the line is not smoothed into a curve or broken into multiple unrelated line segments. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 3 points; if two meet it, add 6 points; if all three meet it, add 9 points)

+3: In the 3 workbooks, S11 chart blue circular markers: A blue circular marker appears at each data point, with a marker diameter of approximately 0.18cm–0.35cm, a blue fill, and a blue or dark blue outline; the number of markers matches the number of data points in the line series. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 3 points; if two meet it, add 6 points; if all three meet it, add 9 points)

+1: In the 3 workbooks, S11 chart horizontal-axis titles: The horizontal-axis title at the bottom of each chart is “Frequency（GHz）” or “Frequency (GHz)”, positioned in the centered area at the bottom of the chart, using Microsoft YaHei, SimSun, or Calibri in a size of 10 points–14 points and in black. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 1 point; if two meet it, add 2 points; if all three meet it, add 3 points)

+1: In the 3 workbooks, S11 chart vertical-axis titles: The vertical-axis title on the left side of each chart is “S11”, positioned in the middle of the left side of the chart, with the text displayed vertically or rotated 90 degrees, using Microsoft YaHei, SimSun, or Calibri in a size of 10 points–14 points and in black. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 1 point; if two meet it, add 2 points; if all three meet it, add 3 points)

+3: In the 3 workbooks, S11 chart horizontal-axis tick marks: The horizontal-axis ticks are arranged in ascending order from the minimum frequency value to the maximum frequency value, with evenly spaced intervals or intervals displayed according to the source-data frequency intervals; the tick labels are “0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24”, in black and in a size of 8 points–12 points; the chart has low frequencies on the left and high frequencies on the right. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 3 points; if two meet it, add 6 points; if all three meet it, add 9 points)

+3: In the 3 workbooks, S11 chart vertical-axis tick marks: The vertical-axis ticks cover the minimum and maximum S11 values in the source data, and the displayed range includes approximately -24 to -8 or a negative-value range close to the data; the tick labels are “-8, -12, -16, -20, -24.”, in black and in a size of 8 points–12 points; values are larger at the top and smaller at the bottom of the vertical axis. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 3 points; if two meet it, add 6 points; if all three meet it, add 9 points)

+1: In the 3 workbooks, S11 chart gray horizontal reference lines: A gray horizontal dashed reference line appears in the upper area of each chart's plot area, positioned approximately near S11=-10 or at the threshold position shown in the task's reference image, with a width of 1 point–1.5 points and a dashed or short-dashed line style, spanning the width of the main plot area from “0” to “24” on the horizontal axis. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 1 point; if two meet it, add 2 points; if all three meet it, add 3 points)

+1: Plot areas of the workbooks' S11 charts: The plot-area background is white or has no fill, with a black or dark gray single solid-line border of 0.75 points–1.25 points; the chart has no dark shading, image background, or unrelated watermark. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 1 point; if two meet it, add 2 points; if all three meet it, add 3 points)

+1: Title areas of the workbooks' S11 charts: The unrelated default title “Chart Title” does not appear at the top of the chart; if a title is set, its text contains “S11 Parameter Curve” or “S11 Curve”, using Microsoft YaHei or Calibri in a size of 16 points–20 points and in black. (If the chart in any one of the 3 files meets this criterion, add 1 point; if two meet it, add 2 points; if all three meet it, add 3 points)
-1: The header row of any table in workbooks 1, 2, or 3 is missing “Frequency（GHz）” and S11（dB）.
-1: The table in workbook 3 has fewer than 28 rows excluding the header row.
-1: In any table in workbooks 1, 2, or 3, excluding the header row, the row height exceeds 19-23 points or the column width exceeds 11-15 points.
